problem.summary: Single-shot detectors put all detection on the deepest ConvNet layer (or on multi-scale maps that add cost), so one layer must cover all object scales and shallow maps lack semantics for small objects; naively combining a deep Residual-101 classifier with SSD, or appending deconvolution layers, does not work out of the box.
statements: A single top-most ConvNet layer carries a great burden to model all possible object scales and shapes.
Shallow layers have less semantic information about objects, so relying on them for small objects can cause low performance on small objects.
Combining multi-scale feature maps increases the memory footprint of a model significantly and decreases the speed of the model.
Neither using the much deeper Residual-101 nor appending deconvolution layers to SSD works out of the box.

evidence.quote: an approach for introducing additional context into state-of-the-art general object detection
it imposes a great burden for a single layer to model all possible object scales and shapes.
which may cause low performance on small objects because shallow layers have less semantic information about objects.
the combined feature map not only increases the memory footprint of a model significantly but also decreases the speed of the model.
Unfortunately neither of these modifications, using the much deeper Residual-101, or adding deconvolution layers to the end of SSD feature layers, work "out of the box".

background.summary: The paper builds on SSD's multi-scale default boxes, Residual-101 as a state-of-the-art classifier, prior use of deconvolution for dense prediction (MS-CNN), multi-layer feature combination (ION, HyperNet), skip connections, and the stacked hourglass structure; the claimed gap is injecting large-scale context into a fast single-shot detector without extra hand-crafted context regions.

relatedWork.name: SSD
relatedWork.relation: the single-shot framework that DSSD augments
relatedWork.quote: SSD [18] spreads out default boxes of different scales to multiple layers within a ConvNet and enforces each layer to focus on predicting objects of certain scale.

relatedWork.name: MS-CNN
relatedWork.relation: prior work using deconvolution to increase feature-map resolution before detection
relatedWork.quote: MS-CNN [2] applies deconvolution on multiple layers of a ConvNet to increase feature map resolution before using the layers to learn region proposals and pool features.

relatedWork.name: R-FCN
relatedWork.relation: state-of-the-art two-stage baseline and source of the stride-reduction trick
relatedWork.quote: Following R-FCN [3], we change the conv5 stage’s effective stride from 32 pixels to 16 pixels to increase feature map resolution.

relatedWork.name: Stacked hourglass networks
relatedWork.relation: structural inspiration for the encoder-decoder side branch
relatedWork.quote: we propose to use an encoder-decoder hourglass structure to pass context information before doing prediction.

evidence.quote: The majority of object detection methods, including SPPnet [13], Fast R-CNN [11], Faster R-CNN [24], RFCN [3] and YOLO [23], use the top-most layer of a ConvNet to learn to detect objects at different scales.

solution.summary: DSSD first swaps SSD's VGG backbone for Residual-101 with an output stride of 16, adds a prediction module (a residual block) before each prediction layer, then adds an asymmetric hourglass deconvolution side branch with feed-forward skip connections and batch normalization, fusing decoder and encoder features by element-wise product before prediction.
solution.approach: Augment a Residual-101-based SSD with a deconvolution hourglass that passes large-scale context down through feed-forward connections and element-wise feature combination before each prediction layer.
components: Residual-101 base network with output stride reduced from 32 to 16 (atrous convolution in conv5)
Prediction module with a residual block before each prediction layer
Asymmetric encoder-decoder hourglass of learned deconvolution layers with skip connections
Batch normalization after each convolution in the deconvolution module
Element-wise product (with element-wise sum as alternative) feature combination
One extra prior-box aspect ratio (1.6) added to (2.0, 3.0)
Two-stage training that freezes the pre-trained SSD weights while training the deconvolution side
Batch-normalization folding into convolution weights at test time

evidence.quote: We then augment SSD+Residual-101 with deconvolution layers to introduce additional large-scale context in object detection and improve accuracy, especially for small objects
The experimental results show that the element-wise product provides the best accuracy
we decide to add one more aspect ratio, 1.6, and use (1.6, 2.0, 3.0) at every prediction layer.

experiments.summary: DSSD is evaluated on PASCAL VOC 2007 test, VOC 2012 test (trained on 07++12), and COCO test-dev2015 against SSD, Faster R-CNN, R-FCN, ION and MR-CNN, with an ablation over prediction modules and deconvolution combination functions; speed is compared on a Titan X with and without batch-normalization layers.

evidence.quote: Our DSSD with 513 × 513 input achieves 81.5% mAP on VOC2007 test, 80.0% mAP on VOC2012 test, and 33.2% mAP on COCO, outperforming a state-of-the-art method R-FCN [3] on each dataset.
SSD513-Residual-101 is already 1.3%(31.2% vs. 29.9%) better than the state-of-the-art method R-FCN [3].
achieves 33.2 % mAP which is 3.3% better than R-FCN [3].
By adding the deconvolution layers on top of SSD321-Residual-101, we can see that it performs better on small objects (7.4% vs. 6.2%)

limitations.summary: DSSD is slower than plain SSD because of the deeper backbone, extra modules and 2.6x more default boxes; the decoder must be trained from scratch, stage-2 fine-tuning hurt performance, deconvolution gave no gain on large objects, and the first prediction layer of Residual-101 predicts weakly.
items: DSSD is not as fast as the original SSD due to Residual-101, extra modules, and more default boxes.
2.6 times more default boxes than SSD slow both prediction and non-maximum suppression.
No pre-trained model exists for the decoder, so its layers start from random initialization.
Adding deconvolution layers improved small-object AP on COCO but gave no improvement on large objects.
Fine-tuning the whole network after the deconvolution module decreased performance.

evidence.quote: The model we proposed is not as fast as the original SSD for multiple reasons.
Table 7 shows that we use 2.6 times more default boxes than a previous version of SSD (43688 vs. 17080).
Since there is no pre-trained model for our decoder, we cannot take the advantage of transfer learning for the decoder layers which must be trained starting from random initialization.
unfortunately we don’t see improvements on large objects.
we did not see any improvements but instead decreased performance.

futureDirections.direction: Find better functions for combining encoder and decoder features beyond the element-wise product.
futureDirections.quote: The better feature combination can be considered as further work to improve the accuracy of the DSSD model.

futureDirections.direction: Speed up DSSD by replacing the learned deconvolution layer with simple bilinear up-sampling.
futureDirections.quote: A potential way to speed up DSSD is to replace the deconvolution layer by a simple bilinear up-sampling.

futureDirections.direction: Extend the encoder-decoder hourglass approach beyond SSD to region-based detectors.
futureDirections.quote: this approach can be applied to other detection methods, such as the R-CNN series methods [12, 11, 24], as well.

futureDirections.direction: Improve the efficiency and effectiveness of encoder-decoder feature combination.
futureDirections.quote: we expect many improvements in finding more efficient and effective ways to combine the features from the encoder and decoder

applications.detail: DSSD improves over SSD in scenes containing small or dense objects, where SSD's small input size fails.
applications.quote: The first case is in scenes containing small objects or dense objects as shown in Figure 4a.

applications.detail: Classes with distinctive context such as tie/man, baseball bat/player, and tennis racket/player are detected more cleanly.
applications.quote: classes with specific relationships can be improved: tie and man in suit, baseball bat and baseball player, soccer ball and soccer player

deploymentClaims: Folding batch-normalization layers into convolution weights improves speed by 1.2x-1.5x and reduces memory footprint up to three times at test time.
DSSD 513 has better accuracy than R-FCN while being only slightly slower; DSSD 321 keeps a speed advantage over R-FCN with a small accuracy drop.
Code and models will be open sourced upon publication.

evidence.quote: We found that this trick improves the speed by 1.2× - 1.5× in general and reduces the memory footprint up to three times.
Compared to R-FCN [3], the SSD 513 model has similar speed and accuracy.
The code will be open sourced with models upon publication.
